1.explanation:
1) parsefiguredivs.lua is the primary pre-render filter that walks Div/Figure AST nodes and turns them into FloatRefTarget. Its parse_float_div and Figure handlers only fire when a user-supplied identifier exists, so unlabeled subimages never become subfloats nor get auto-IDs.

2) common/figures.lua defines isFigureDiv and discoverFigure logic that determines which Divs or Paras count as figures. It requires explicit fig-cap attributes or existing captions/IDs, so multi-column Divs with unlabeled images slip through and aren’t parsed as subfigures.

3) crossref/figures.lua skips any FloatRefTarget with no identifier (i.e. is_unlabeled_float), so even if a float were created, it wouldn’t be indexed or rendered with subcaptions. Together, these prevent unlabeled subimages from being auto-labeled and subcaptioned.
1.bug_scenario: When a multi-column figure Div contains two images without explicit IDs, Quarto’s LaTeX filter generates them as two separate top-level floats (Figure 1: Surus and Figure 2: Hanno), and then the parent as Figure 3, instead of subcaptions (a) and (b) under a single figure. Only when the user provides IDs on the subimages does Quarto emit \subcaption and proper sub-figure labels. Thus, unlabeled subfigures aren’t being auto–identified as subfloats and don’t get subcaptions.
